Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent 504s and long tail latency spikes hitting our API surface this morning. Symptoms:
- 99.9th p latency jumped from ~1.2s to 8-12s between 10:00-11:30 UTC yesterday and again today.
- A small subset (~0.6%) of requests timeout with 504. Error rate for that window spiked to 0.9%.
- Throughput during spike appears constant, no sudden traffic surge on our end.

Sample errors attached (acme_request_samples.log). We are on your hosted API (api-redwood-1), model pinned to rwd-3b-quant, traffic comes from multiple regions but most impacted requests are US-east.

Can someone confirm if there were infra changes, throttling, or autoscaler events on your side? This is affecting a customer-facing workflow — need a response within the hour.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Production: intermittent timeouts — Redwood API

Quick technical summary from runtime team after first pass:
- We see repeated episodes where per-GPU request queues climb above 64 entries for a short burst; once queueing >64, the scheduler begins delaying assignment which increases tail latency.
- Autoscaler logs show bursts of scale activity but a hard concurrency cap of 16 active requests per GPU instance is being hit. When the cap is hit, new requests are queued rather than immediately scheduled.
- KV-cache thrashing observed for sequences >1024 tokens for this customer's workload: cache invalidation + cache misses amplify execution time of individual requests.

Immediate mitigation options (recommended order):
1) Temporary concurrency cap bump from 16 -> 24 for the dedicated pool serving Acme (safe for 2h)
2) Route heavy requests to rwd-3b-quant-lowlat (lower memory but faster attention kernels) for 30 min while we stabilize
3) Enable more aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated session IDs for Acme (if acceptable from correctness POV)

I attached the raw runtime metrics and a quick GPU heap/GPU utilization snapshot. If we have sign-off I can run the concurrency bump and routing change now — this should reduce 99.9p quickly while we do a deeper RCA.

-Evelyn

-Jonas

Go ahead executed: increased concurrency cap for Acme pool 16->24 and enabled routing rule to rwd-3b-quant-lowlat for the flagged session IDs.
Observed impact within ~6 minutes:
- 99.9p latency reduced from ~9.6s to ~3.2s for impacted requests in the sample window.
- 504 count dropped to near-zero for the last 30m window.

I'm attaching a short post-mitigation summary. We'll keep the bump in place while we finish the RCA; Evelyn's team will dig into why queueing spiked (autoscaler responsiveness vs transient hot-sharding on a few GPUs).

-Rishi

Mina / Samir — following up after our mitigation and initial RCA work:

Summary so far:
- Immediate action: temporary concurrency cap bump and routing to a lower-latency variant reduced tail latency and eliminated 504s.
- Preliminary root cause: a combination of short-lived request hot-shards that created per-GPU queueing >64 and KV-cache invalidation for long sequences; autoscaler reacted but there was a small window where queued requests accumulated.

Next steps:
- Evelyn's team will complete a deeper RCA (kernel selection traces, scheduling delays, and autoscaler tuning) and share a full report by EOD 2026-01-23.
- We'll propose a permanent mitigation: adaptive concurrency caps per-pool and a scheduler change to prioritize low-latency requests (RFC in drive link).
- Schedule a 30-minute postmortem with your team: https://calendar.redwood/meet/2026-01-22-queueing-incident (I put tentative 10:00 AM PST).

We will also propose a goodwill credit from CS once RCA is complete — I'll coordinate and follow up. Sorry for the disruption and thank you for the quick signal and logs — that made mitigation straightforward.

Best,
Jonas Weber
